newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel cabinet meets on capital market reforms.
newsitem.headline: Israel cabinet meets on capital market reforms.

text.p: A tax on short-term savings is crucial for reforming Israel's capital market, Treasury Director General David Brodett said on Sunday as the cabinet began debate on a package of reform measures.

The tax is by far the most controversial of the measures recommended by a panel headed by Brodett that aim to increase long-term savings. The committee was formed in the wake of a collapse in bond prices in July.
The cabinet meeting is expected to conclude by 1100 GMT. It is not known whether the cabinet will vote on the measures or hold further debate at a later date.

Aides to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu have said he does not support taxes on savings of less than 10 years, as proposed by Brodett. The only minister to come out publicly in support is Immigration Minister Yuli Edelstein.

The other Brodett recommendations are not expected to encounter strong opposition. These include measures that would restrict sales of special high-yield government bonds to pension funds and reduce the tax rate on dividends.
